title: POC weekly sync - onboarding & env readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review initial benchmark results, confirm infra access (VPC/SSH/KMS), discuss tuning (batching, KV cache, quant), and agree next steps for dedicated benchmark run and security checklist.
next_steps: Redwood to run 1-hour dedicated benchmark with BlueFin test prompts (Priya) - schedule for next Tue
Send security pack (SOC2 summary, network diagram, KMS details) to Anna - Jordan
Provide dedicated GPU SKU/pricing and pilot contract template - Jordan
BlueFin to provide sample traffic profile and sanitized prompt set - Sara
Set up VPC peering and service account access for Redwood test cluster - David
action_items: Priya (SE) - Run dedicated 1-hour benchmark using BlueFin prompts and share token-level latency/cost breakdown (due 2026-04-14)
Jordan (AE) - Send security pack + pricing + pilot contract template (due 2026-04-10)
David (Infra) - Provide VPC CIDR and create service account with minimum IAM for tests (due 2026-04-09)
Sara (ML) - Sanitize and share 200 sample prompts and expected outputs for quality checks (due 2026-04-12)
Anna (Security) - Confirm required compliance docs and whether a NDA amendment is needed (due 2026-04-11)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Mike (CTO, BlueFin): Mike here.
[00:12] Sara (ML Eng): Sara on.
[00:14] David (Infra): David.
[00:15] Anna (Security): Anna here.
[00:18] Priya (SE, Redwood): Priya here, good morning.
[00:22] Jordan: Cool. Agenda for 30-45 min: onboarding updates, results review, tuning items, and actions. We ran the initial hosted pass last week and have some numbers. Priya do you want to start with infra/access status?
[02:05] Priya: Sure. On the Redwood side, we requested VPC peering details and a service account key to spin up the test runner in BlueFin's VPC. David, I saw your note that you're creating a role with limited IAM. Any blockers?
[02:28] David: We're almost done — will create the service account and add the VPN/VPC peering rules. One question: do you need full SSH to any hosts or just the endpoint? We prefer minimal surface area.
[02:42] Priya: Endpoint access only, plus egress to our model RPC endpoints. We'll use mTLS and the service account. We'll also need the KMS key ARN to encrypt logs and any cached artifacts.
[03:05] Anna: On that KMS piece, we need to see key usage policies and rotation. Can you include KMS logs in the security pack?
[03:18] Jordan: Yes, we'll include key rotation and CloudTrail examples in the pack. I'll own that deliverable.
[05:00] Priya: Quick update on the initial benchmark we ran on hosted infra: we ran 1000 sample prompts from the seed set Sara provided. Median p50 latency was ~260ms per token at the prompt lengths you gave, p95 around 780ms. Cost per 1k tokens estimate was shared in the sheet. We saw a couple of long-tail outliers tied to cold KV cache misses.
[05:35] Sara: Interesting, did you separate prefix caching vs full KV cache misses? We saw variability on conversational threads.
[05:46] Priya: We instrumented prefix cache hits but not full persistent KV cache in that run — that was on the hosted flow where caching is warm per session but not shared. For the dedicated benchmark we'll enable KV cache warmup and persistent cache to mimic production.
[06:15] Jordan: We also ran a quick quantized variant test — dropping to 4-bit quant helped cost but we noted a small degradation in some summarization outputs. Sara, is that acceptable for your use case?
[06:30] Sara: For extraction tasks maybe okay, but for summarization we need fidelity. We need the quality/regression numbers.
[06:41] Priya: We'll run A/B comparisons and provide the accuracy deltas on your eval set.
[08:00] Mike: Timeline-wise, our goal is decision by end of month. We want to validate latency and output quality before we sign for dedicated capacity. Also need SSO and audit logs to match SOC2 requirements.
[08:22] Jordan: Understood. We'll prioritize the security docs. Carlos will also prepare an onboarding checklist for Dedicated.
[09:05] David: Regarding network, are you doing NAT traversal or do we need to open specific ports?
[09:12] Priya: No unusual ports — outbound HTTPS to our endpoints and the peering link. We'll share a minimal list.
[10:00] [brief crosstalk] Anna: Also, retention policy — we need confirmation on message retention, logs and PII handling. What does Redwood retain during a POC?
[10:23] Jordan: By default for hosted POCs we keep logs for 30 days, but we can configure retention and persistence for dedicated. We'll include retention controls in the security pack.
[11:30] Priya: Back to tuning: batching and max latency. In the hosted run we used a conservative batch window. For dedicated, we can tune continuous batching aggressiveness — reduce per-token cost but may push p95 up. We can simulate with your traffic profile.
[12:05] Sara: Our production traffic is spiky, with bursts of short prompts (3-5 tokens) and occasional long summarizations (500-700 tokens). We'll send the distribution.
[13:00] Priya: Great. For spikes we recommend a combination of a small burst pool and autoscale + model routing to a cheaper variant for non-critical requests. That will require canary routing rules which we can set up.
[14:20] Mike: On data security, will the model weights or artifacts be stored in our VPC? We prefer on-prem isolation if possible.
[14:34] Jordan: For Dedicated you can have model artifacts pinned in your VPC or we can run an on-prem package. We'll detail options — dedicated GPU pools vs private on-prem.
[16:00] Priya: The dedicated benchmark we'll run next week will be on a reserved GPU pool we control but with network isolation so the traffic stays in your VPC. We'll mount KMS-managed keys for any persisted caches.
[17:05] David: Sounds good. For the service account, what minimum IAM permissions do you need?
[17:18] Priya: Read/write to a specific storage bucket for model cache, permission to create ephemeral compute instances in the peered subnet, and KMS encrypt/decrypt for the test key. We'll publish an example IAM policy.
[18:30] Sara: On the quality side, one of our concerns is hallucination on long-context summarization. Can you run the regression eval against our golden set and include precision/recall and ROUGE?
[18:50] Priya: Yes, we'll include ROUGE, BLEU where appropriate, and a manual spot-check for hallucination cases. We'll send a short report with examples.
[20:00] Jordan: We also noticed a tokenization mismatch with one of your prompt templates — some system tokens were double-escaped. That caused a small delta in token counts and cost. Sara, can you confirm your prompt template?
[20:20] Sara: Ah, yeah we have a preprocessor that wraps some tags. I'll sanitize and share.
[22:00] Priya: Regarding quantization: we tested 8-bit and 4-bit. 8-bit gave a near-zero quality hit and 4-bit had a noticeable drop on summarization. For cost-savings, 8-bit q8 is our recommended starting point for BlueFin's workload.
[23:00] Mike: If 8-bit is near-zero quality hit, what's the cost delta compared to fp16?
[23:12] Priya: Roughly 20-30% lower per-token cost depending on batch size and kernel paths. We'll put exact numbers in the benchmark sheet.
[25:00] Jordan: On SLA and uptime, once you're on Dedicated we offer an SLA with measured p99 and service credits. We'll include sample SLA language in the pilot contract.
[26:10] Anna: For audit readiness, can you provide exportable audit logs for user-level actions and API keys? We need to ingest them into our SIEM.
[26:28] Carlos (CSM): Yes, we provide audit logs and can deliver them to your syslog or S3 forwarder; we'll include the format and retention options in the security pack.
[28:00] Priya: A small note: we hit a few outliers in the hosted run due to stateful KV cache cold starts — for long conversation workloads the cache warmup is important. In dedicated we can pre-warm caches using a synthetic preload.
[29:10] Sara: Can you simulate warm cache behavior in the dedicated benchmark? That would be ideal.
[29:20] Priya: Absolutely — the benchmark will include a warmup phase. We'll run two passes: cold and warm, and share separate metrics.
[30:45] Mike: Good. On procurement — finance will need the pricing sheet and an indicative monthly commit for dedicated. Jordan, can you get that?
[30:56] Jordan: Yep, I'll send the pricing and commitment options.
[31:30] David: A technical Q: does Redwood support model rollback in the serving runtime if a new model variant causes regressions?
[31:42] Priya: Yes — we have automatic rollbacks and canary routing. We also keep model versioning so you can pin a version per route.
[33:00] Sara: One more on metrics: can we get token-level cost by route and per-tenant?
[33:12] Priya: Yep that's exposed in the Console — token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and per-route dashboards. We'll share sample screenshots.
[34:20] Anna: If we go to Private/on-prem later, what changes in your support model?
[34:35] Jordan: Support levels are similar but with an enterprise license; there's an installation window and a short knowledge transfer. We'll reflect that in the contract template.
[35:50] Priya: Any blockers from your side for the dedicated benchmark next week?
[36:00] David: Only the service account and the VPC peering — I'll prioritize those.
[36:12] Sara: We'll finalize the sanitized prompts and the expected outputs by Monday.
[36:20] Anna: I'll review the security pack once it's sent and respond with any additional controls.
[37:00] Jordan: Great. Recap: Redwood runs dedicated benchmark (Priya), security pack + pricing (Jordan), BlueFin provides prompts and infra details (Sara/David), Anna will confirm compliance needs.
[37:22] Jordan: Any other questions?
[37:30] Mike: No, that's all. Thanks.
[37:35] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and send the documents.
[38:00] [meeting ends]
notes: Recorded a hosted baseline and planned a dedicated benchmark; security pack requested; action items assigned. Transcript includes some auto-transcription imperfections (tokenization -> tokkenization noted in internal logs).
